Save $5,000 in 26 paydays, starting Fri Oct 23. Here's the whole plan.

1. Pick a separate place for it, away from everyday spending, and give it a name.
2. Set an automatic transfer for payday: $192.31, or your own pace.
3. Write down your finish-line date. On this plan it's payday 26: Fri Oct 8, 2027.

The math: 25 paydays of $192.31, then $192.25 on payday 26 = exactly $5,000.00. Halfway is payday 13 (Fri Apr 9, 2027).
Not $192.31 for you? $100 a payday gets there in 50 paydays. $250 gets there in 20.
A sample plan, not real results. Same amount every payday, no windfalls. Miss one? We'll show the catch-up math.
Every second Friday at 12 pm ET: the progress bar, one real-number lesson (Canada and US) and one move for that payday.

Follow @fullyfundedhq so you don't miss payday 1. Run your own numbers in the free Paycheque Split Calculator, link in bio.

Source: sample-plan arithmetic, no outside figures · As of Oct 2026

General education only, not financial advice.

Plan one potluck menu that works for every diet at the table. Paste your guest list and one prompt.

1. List who's coming, their diets and what each person offered to bring.
2. Paste the list with the prompt below.
3. Confirm every allergy with the guest before anyone cooks.

In our example (9 guests, 4 diets) it gave every dish an owner, checked each guest's plate and flagged what's easy to miss: soy sauce usually contains wheat, regular oats are often cross-contaminated and vanilla extract contains alcohol.

PROMPT (copy and paste):
I'm hosting a potluck for 9. Here's who's coming, their diets, and what they offered to bring: [guest list]. Plan one menu so everyone gets a full plate, give each dish to someone who offered it, and flag hidden ingredients to watch for.

Allergies are serious. Always confirm with the guest and read the label on anything store-bought.

posts.caption:
Get up to $2,000 for your kid's school, free. Here's how to claim the Canada Learning Bond.

1. Get your child a SIN (Social Insurance Number).
2. Open an RESP, a school savings account, with a provider that offers the bond. No deposit needed.
3. Ask for the bond when you open it. Already have an RESP? Ask if the bond was requested.

How much: $500 for the first eligible year, then $100 for each later eligible year up to age 15. Maximum $2,000. ESDC also pays $25 to help cover the cost of opening the RESP.
Who: kids born in 2004 or later from lower-income families. One eligible year is enough for the first $500 (Jul 2025 to Jun 2026: 1 to 3 kids, adjusted family income $57,375 or less).
ESDC estimates about two-thirds of those born in 2004 or after are eligible for at least $500. It only lands once someone asks for it.
Turned 18? You can apply yourself until the day before you turn 21. It applies in Quebec too.
Can you add $500 a year? The education savings grant adds 20%, plus 20% more on the first $500 if family income is $58,523 or less (2026).

Send this to a parent, or to anyone 18 to 20.

Source: canada.ca · Rules as of Oct 2026

General education only, not financial advice.

#resp #canadalearningbond #personalfinancecanada #parenting #moneytips

posts.caption:
Never guess a parking sign again. Snap the whole pole and ask one question.

1. Take one clear photo of the whole pole, straight on.
2. Paste the prompt below with your exact day and time.
3. Find the part of the sign it quotes before you walk away.

In our example (Tuesday at 4:40 pm) it said no, not even stopping, until 6:00 pm. Then it laid out the whole week from the same photo and flagged that the sign never says when "overnight" starts.

PROMPT (copy and paste):
[photo of the sign] It's [day], [time]. Can I park here? If not, when can I, and for how long? Quote the part of the sign you're using.

City rules for holidays, street cleaning and snow routes may not be on the sign, so check your city's rules too.

posts.caption:
Turning down a raise? Check your benefit lines first. It takes 3 steps.

1. List the benefits your household gets that depend on income.
2. For each one, ask: does it trim a little per dollar, or stop at a line?
3. Compare the raise after tax with what you'd lose. Use family income: a partner's raise counts.

Tax brackets can't cost you the raise. Cross Canada's $58,523 line by $1 and the extra tax on that dollar is 6.5 cents. US: 10 cents at $50,400 of taxable income.
Some benefits can. Canada's Dental Care Plan (only if you have no access to dental insurance): family net income under $70,000, you pay 0% of plan fees. At $70,000, 40%. At $80,000, 60%. At $90,000, you're not covered.
The Canada Child Benefit trims instead: one child, family income $60,000 to $62,000 means $140 less a year, from next July.
US: the marketplace premium tax credit is for income from 100% to 400% of the poverty line. One person on a 2026 plan: $62,600. Medicaid and SNAP limits vary by state.

Send this to whoever turned down hours over a benefit.

Sources: canada.ca, irs.gov, healthcare.gov · Rules as of Oct 2026

General education only, not financial advice.

#taxbrackets #personalfinancecanada #personalfinance #dentalcare #moneytips

posts.caption:
Earn over $69K? Your fall cheques get bigger. Here's how to plan for it.

1. Find year-to-date CPP and EI on your pay stub. The 2026 max is $1,123.07 for EI and $4,230.45 for CPP.
2. Mark the pay where they stop. At $100,000 paid every 2 weeks, EI ends on pay 18 and CPP on pay 20.
3. Give the bump a job: set a transfer for it from that pay on, and keep budgeting on the January cheque.

Why: CPP and EI only come off your pay up to a yearly limit. 2026: EI stops after $68,900 of earnings, CPP after $74,600, CPP2 after $85,000.
At $100,000, from pay 24 that's $283.53 less taken off each cheque than in January. Income tax can tick up a little, so take-home grows slightly less.
Under $69K? Your deductions run all year, so your cheque stays steady.
US: Social Security (6.2%) stops at $184,500. At $200K, that's +$476.92 on the last 2 cheques.
Quebec: QPP replaces CPP and EI is 1.30%, but the same idea applies.

See where each cheque goes, fall bump included: free Paycheque Split Calculator, link in bio.

Sources: canada.ca, ssa.gov · Rules as of Oct 2026

General education only, not financial advice.

Get answers about your lease that you can check. Add one line to your question.

1. Paste your lease, with names and addresses removed.
2. Add the line below, then ask your questions.
3. Find each quote in your lease, word for word. No match? Don't rely on that answer.

On our example lease it quoted §9 for subletting and §17 for pets, and said "Not in the document" when we asked about a rent increase. All 5 quotes matched the lease, word for word.

PROMPT (copy and paste):
For each answer, quote the exact sentence from my document. If it isn't in the document, say "Not in the document." Don't fill gaps with general rules. [paste your document] [your questions]

It cuts down made-up answers; it doesn't end them. Local laws can override what a lease says.

posts.caption:
Laid off tomorrow? Find your savings gap tonight, in 3 steps.

1. Estimate your weekly EI: 55% of your average insurable weekly earnings, up to $729 a week in 2026, before tax.
2. Check how many weeks: 14 to 45, depending on where you live and how many hours you worked.
3. Take six months of costs, minus EI for your weeks. What's left is your gap.

Example: $4,800 a month in costs, six months off work ($28,800). If EI lasts 26 weeks, your savings cover $9,846. If it lasts 14 weeks, $18,594. If you don't qualify, all $28,800.
You hit the $729 cap at $68,900 a year. At $100,000, that's $729 of about $1,923 a week: 38%.
Tip: EI is taxable, so add a cushion. For claims starting by Oct 9, 2027, there's no waiting week and severance isn't deducted. Quebec: same EI rules for job loss.

Send this to the friend bracing for layoffs.

Source: canada.ca · Rules as of Oct 2026

General education only, not financial advice.

#emergencyfund #personalfinancecanada #layoffs #employmentinsurance #budgeting

See everything your renewal changed, not just the price. Paste last year's letter next to this year's.

1. Find last year's renewal. Check your email or your insurer's app.
2. Paste both letters with the prompt below.
3. Match each change to the letters before you decide anything.

In our example it found the $228 increase plus 4 more changes on pages 2 to 4: a higher collision deductible, rental-car cover removed, an ended discount and a new $3 monthly fee. It also noticed the letter never explains the $228.

PROMPT (copy and paste):
Compare these two renewal letters. List every change: what it was, what it is now, which page. Include fees, deductibles and anything removed. Don't give advice. Then list questions I should ask.

It compares; the coverage decisions are yours. Take your questions to your insurer or broker.

Get your family's week on one page, with the clashes flagged. Paste both calendars and one prompt.

1. Paste both calendars, the school notes and the week's texts.
2. Add the prompt below.
3. Check every line against your calendars before you rely on it.

In our example week it found that nobody was free for Thursday's swim pickup, and that Grandma's lunch landed at the same time as the school fair.

This is week 1 of our new series, 12 Weeks, 12 Automations. Every Monday at 1 pm ET we hand one life-admin job to AI and show the real prompt and the real output. By Jan 4, 2027 you'll have 12 saved prompts for jobs you stop starting from scratch. You paste, it drafts, you check.
The 12 jobs: 1 the Sunday week-ahead brief · 2 dinners for busy nights + grocery list · 3 school emails → dates, forms, money · 4 monthly bill and subscription check · 5 returns and warranties tracker · 6 gift list with buy-by dates · 7 group money, settled · 8 holiday hosting plan · 9 appointment prep sheet · 10 the firm, polite refund email · 11 renewal compare · 12 home maintenance, month by month.

PROMPT (copy and paste):
Here's everything for our family this week: two calendars, school notes and texts. Make a week-ahead brief: for each day, who's doing what and what to pack or pay. Then flag any clashes or anything nobody is covering. Don't invent anything that isn't here.
